bug_semantics: In `anyquery server` (MySQL-protocol TCP listener, default port 8070), the SQLite namespace used by every client connection registers built-in virtual-table modules (`json_reader`/`csv_reader`, later `log_reader` and other `read_*` modules) that take a caller-supplied path/URL and open it through `hashicorp/go-getter` with no directory allowlist. Auth is optional: if neither AuthFile nor Users is set, the server accepts any connection. A remote client can therefore `CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE ... USING csv_reader('/etc/passwd')` (or `json_reader` / `log_reader` / `file=...`) and `SELECT` the contents of any file the server process can read. Default `--host` is loopback, but `--host 0.0.0.0` (the advisory PoC) exposes the sink on the network with no sandbox.
flaw_origin: The MySQL server command already existed (3993837954bf7e23de54703d740ee76f6df02a59, 2024-06-16) and executed client SQL against a shared namespace with no auth by default, but it had no file-reading virtual tables. edfe9dcb68ffcf6c5832c5f2f6a1ef79909ed6e6 (2024-06-26, '✨ Add JSON and CSV tables') is the first write of that sink: it added `module/helper.go` `downloadFile`/`openMmapedFile` (unrestricted go-getter Client on the user path), `CsvModule`/`JSONModule` that call it, and `namespace.Register` `CreateModule("json_reader"/"csv_reader")` with empty structs. From that commit, server-mode clients inherit the modules. Positional `csv_reader('/path')` matching the published PoC was added two days later in df4b967a320ec9dee6ea1556a9ae7fdb398a797b; `json_reader` already used `args[3]` as the path in the BIC. No path policy existed until 0.4.5 sandboxing.
